Approval checkpoints pause the agent before external messages, payments, deletions, or irreversible changes.
Coordination needs clear roles, shared state, handoff rules, conflict resolution, and one accountable owner.
Cost controls set budgets, cache repeated work, choose smaller tools first, and report spend.
Evaluate agents with task success, error rate, approval quality, cost, latency, and user satisfaction.
Guardrails: allowed tools, approval points, spending limits, data boundaries, logging, and stop conditions.
Handoff should include goal, progress, evidence, blockers, and the exact decision needed.
Log goals, tool calls, decisions, approvals, errors, and outcomes without storing secrets.
On error, an agent should stop risky actions, record what happened, try safe recovery, and ask for help when unsure.
Privacy controls limit data access, mask sensitive fields, set retention, and record every disclosure.
Stop conditions include missing data, policy conflict, repeated failure, budget limit, and user cancellation.
Tool permissions should be narrow, time-limited when possible, logged, and separated by task.
